citation: Aho, Kevin. "Heidegger on Melancholia, Deep Boredom, and the Inability-to-Be." Philosophy, Psychiatry, & Psychology 27, no. 3 (September 2020): 215–217.
thesis: Heidegger's FCM account of profound/deep boredom (tiefe Langeweile), introduced two years after Being and Time, illuminates the same desynchronized, meaning-stripped temporality that Emily Hughes diagnoses in major depression as ontological 'dying' (Sterben); via Heidegger's later 'turn' (Kehre) toward historical ground moods (Grundstimmungen), profound boredom can further be read as the possible ground mood of modernity itself rather than a brain disorder.

sections.title: Framing Hughes: melancholia as ontological death
sections.summary: Hughes's account of major depression as ontological 'dying' (Sterben): temporal desynchronization strips intelligibility from the world, leaving the sufferer 'unable to live and unable to die.'

sections.title: Being and Time backdrop
sections.summary: Temporality (Zeitlichkeit), thrown projection (geworfen Entwurf), and the disclosive unity of time as background architecture; therapy restores future-orientation and 'ability-to-be.'

sections.title: The stakes of physician-assisted suicide
sections.summary: Assisted death forecloses ontological death's potentially liberating rupture from tranquilized everydayness ('the They'/das Man).

sections.title: Turn to FCM's profound boredom
sections.summary: Tiefe Langeweile introduced as a parallel register to melancholia: bored not by a particular thing but by 'everything'; an atemporal limbo, the mood as 'insidious creature.'

sections.title: The Kehre and historical ground moods
sections.summary: Grundstimmungen of entire epochs (Hellenistic 'wonder'/Erstaunen vs. modern disenchantment); depression reframed as the ground mood of modernity, not an inner/chemical condition.

sections.title: Closing ambivalence
sections.summary: The epochal 'nihilating space' holds a possible collective 'new beginning' (neuer Anfang), but Heidegger's own doubt is left standing ('only a God can save us').

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: primary organizing construct; glossed via Heidegger's 'elevated beyond the particular situation' formula

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: contrastive only, via situational examples (boring book/drive/airport-wait); not named as a 'form'

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: contrast of particular-situation-bound boredom vs. world-as-a-whole boredom

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: modern world 'bleached out' of enchantment; things reduced to equal/indifferent value

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: central connective construct: desynchronization/atemporal-limbo shared by melancholia and profound boredom

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: qualified, existential-disclosive sense only — nihilating space opening onto authentic self-recovery/new beginning, not an evolutionary-regulatory account

readings.claim: Profound boredom (FCM) and melancholic 'dying' (Hughes, via BT) share a phenomenological structure of desynchronized, meaning-stripped temporality.
Profound boredom opens a 'nihilating space' that can rupture tranquilized everydayness ('the They'), analogous to BT's anxiety.
Via the Kehre, boredom is not only an individual mood but can be the ground mood (Grundstimmung) of an entire historical epoch.
Modern depression, read as the ground mood of modernity, is not reducible to a brain disorder or chemical imbalance.
The epochal nihilating space holds potential for a collective 'new beginning,' though Heidegger remains ambivalent whether this will occur.

interlocutors.name: Hughes, Emily
interlocutors.role: primary interlocutor — 'Melancholia, temporal disruption, and the torment of being both unable to live and unable to die'

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin — Being and Time
interlocutors.role: background architecture (temporality, anxiety, das Man, ontological death)

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin — Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
interlocutors.role: primary phenomenological source for profound boredom

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin — post-Kehre texts (Introduction to Metaphysics; Basic Questions of Philosophy; "Messkirch's Seventh Centennial"; Der Spiegel interview)
interlocutors.role: source of epochal ground-mood material extending beyond FCM

tensions.axis: individual-Dasein mood (BT/FCM) vs. epoch-level historical ground mood (post-Kehre)
tensions.note: is depression/profound boredom an individual pathology or a civilizational condition? Aho moves between both without fully reconciling scale.

tensions.axis: existential-disclosive account of boredom's 'positive' function vs. reductive biomedical/chemical-imbalance model
tensions.note: Aho explicitly rejects the latter; the piece does not engage empirical psychiatry beyond this rejection.

tensions.axis: hope (new beginning) vs. ambivalence (Heidegger's own doubt)
tensions.note: closing lines leave the possibility of epochal transformation unresolved.
